correctness.summary: The exact IO-code formula is correct. Pendant supports are forced into every code. The remaining vertices partition into p blocks B_v of size Delta+1, and every possible pair of omissions inside a single B_v either empties a degree-two neighborhood or makes two code traces equal, so at most one vertex per block can be omitted. Conversely, omitting exactly the original skeleton vertices leaves support-leaf and paired-subdivision edges; every noncenter has a distinct singleton trace and every center has its distinct Delta-element neighborhood, giving a code of size |V|-p. The order formula follows from the handshaking sum. Any cycle in the lift is three times a skeleton cycle, so no 4-cycle occurs. Independent brute-force optimization on lifts of P2, P3, and C3 at Delta=3 returned the exact predicted optima 10,14,12.

independent_checks: Reconstructed every omission-incompatibility case in a block B_v.
Verified the explicit all-noncenter IO-code and the structural properties of the lift.
Brute-forced three small lifted graphs independently and recovered the theorem's exact gamma_IOC values.
Inspected the 2026 open-access paper's Remark 14 and confirmed its stated open target.
limitations: The exact asymptotic extremal constant remains unknown.
The construction does not characterize all extremal graphs or prove the known upper bound asymptotically sharp.
For Delta=3, a known 5/6 family is stronger than this construction's limiting 4/5 density.
Older tree literature using different construction language remains a residual originality risk.

originality.summary: The open-access 2026 Chakraborty--Foucaud--Henning article proves the general (2Delta-1)/(2Delta) upper bound and gives a lower construction of density (2Delta-4)/(2Delta-3), with a small refinement. Its Remark 14 explicitly says the authors did not obtain ratios as high as (2Delta-3)/(2Delta-2) and leave that as an open problem. The audited cycle-skeleton family has the strictly larger density (2Delta-2)/(2Delta-1), while the path lift gives trees tending to the same density. Searches across identifying-open-code and equivalent OLD terminology did not locate the general twice-subdivided skeleton formula. Older tree literature under different construction language remains the main priority risk.

scientific_value.summary: For every Delta>=4 the construction improves beyond the ratio explicitly proposed as an open target in a 2026 paper and narrows the asymptotic construction-to-upper-bound gap to 1/[2Delta(2Delta-1)]. The exact arbitrary-skeleton formula is also reusable beyond the cycle example.
